states.changed: A reader meets every incident of the AI Incident Database as bars by year, can colour them by who wrote the first report, where the failure sits and whether a public act is on record, and finds step 2's 29 public acts looked for in the record, four of them found.

A reader meets the 58 self-published first reports as squares read by hand (the harmed wrote 21), and the 176 answered incidents as squares to colour by who answered, whom a public act lands on and where the failure sits, each opening to what was answered.

A reader meets the check: every hand-read item coded a second time and the two readings side by side, 120 press reports nobody had read as squares (the harmed wrote 4), a table of all 60 public acts with body, act and date, and an answer corrected from 50 public acts to 60 and from a floor of 21 to an estimate of 77.

A reader meets the paper's own figures: bars of who wrote first when it was not the press, year by year; the 37 first reports on a public body's address as squares (19 announce an act, 9 of them new, so the floor rises from 62 to 71); the 23 on the maker's own address (13 about a failure of its own system, 9 of those in 2026); and a table of who submitted the reports, one name on 61.9 % of them.

A reader meets a dated correction: all 69 public acts as squares to switch between the page as presented and as corrected, seven of them marked (four acts are only begun, not concluded; three went in favour of the party they land on), each opening to the sentence of the report it rests on, and the table of acts and the answer corrected to 30 concluded of 60.
